subtitulo: Compressing without distorting, for an audience without your context
descripcion: Summarising is a mediation skill, not a comprehension skill: the test is whether your listener can now act, not whether you understood. At C1 the difficulty is selection under constraint — deciding what to drop, and being able to say what you dropped. The structural move is top-down: conclusion first, then two or three supports, then the caveat.

ejemplos.texto: *The short version is that the course works, but only for people who already have the basics.*
*I'm skipping the methodology. Ask me if you want it.*
*That's the finding. My own view is that they measured the wrong thing.*
*Three things came out of it. And the one that actually matters is the third.*
*The sample was small, so treat it as directional.*
*That's what they found. What I think about it is another matter.*

notas: Saying what you left out converts a lossy summary into a trustworthy one.
Keep reporting and evaluating separate. *They found X* and *I think X is wrong* must not blur.
The order events happened is almost never the right order to explain them.
errores: Chronological retelling instead of a summary.
*Resume* meaning *summarise* — false friend; it means to restart.
Compressing by removing words rather than content: dense and unreadable.
Losing hedging in compression, turning a tentative finding into a fact.

mision.consigna: Summarise something long you actually read or watched this month, for someone with no background in it.
requisitos: conclusion in the first two sentences

microtareas.texto: Summarise a work document in exactly 50 words. Count them.
Same document, 15 words. Notice what you were forced to drop.
Record 90 seconds summarising an article, conclusion first.

autochequeo: Is my conclusion in the first two sentences?
Did I retell chronologically instead of summarising?
Did I say what I left out?
Did compression turn any tentative finding into a flat fact?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on summarising. (1) Is the conclusion in the first two sentences? (2) Did I retell chronologically instead of summarising? (3) Did compression turn a tentative claim into a fact? (4) Where would someone with no background get lost? Do not rewrite the text.

filas: Give me two minutes and I'll take you through it
*The short version is…* / *If you only remember one thing…*
Three things came out of it. First… Second… And the one that matters…
I'm skipping the methodology — ask if you want it
The sample was small, so treat it as directional
That's what they found. What I think about it is…

contraste.es: Spanish academic and professional prose often builds bottom-up, with the conclusion last. English expects the answer at the top. Transferring the Spanish shape makes an English summary read as evasive rather than thorough.
